prompt:
Let $f(x)=x^{3}-6x^{2}+9x+1$.

**(a)** Write down the $y$-intercept. **[1]**

**(b)** Find the coordinates of the local maximum and local minimum points. **[2]**

**(c)** Find the zero of $f$. **[1]**

**(d)** Hence state the number of solutions of $f(x)=3$. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $(0,1)$ **(A1)**

**(b)** Local maximum $(1,5)$, local minimum $(3,1)$ **(A1)(A1)** (from the GDC, or $f'(x)=3(x-1)(x-3)$)

**(c)** $x\approx-0.104$ **(A1)**

**(d)** The line $y=3$ lies between the minimum value 1 and the maximum value 5, so it crosses the graph three times: **3** solutions **(R1)**
